item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.28
item.description:
Tessera no longer shuffles your windows when an app shows a small alert or progress window.
- Windows that can't be resized, such as Finder's "can't be completed" alerts and About boxes, are never pulled into a split. A run of alerts beside a split no longer makes the windows next to them shrink and grow back each time. - Short-lived windows that can't zoom, such as Finder's Copy progress window, no longer join a split as they appear and close. - Tile All Windows leaves windows that can't be resized where they are.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.27
item.description:
Tessera now uses less memory and does less work while you use it.
- Closing Settings or the welcome window now frees the memory it used. Settings opens on the same page with your search and window position kept. Text half-typed in a filter or a new theme name is cleared. - Tips free their memory once they fade out. - The Ring does less work as you move the mouse. - A smaller app download and a smaller command-line tool.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.26
item.description: - Settings has a live stage beside the panes. It acts out what you point at, and you can drag the ring to resize it, drag column edges and split seams, and pick preview fills from pictures. On narrow screens the stage folds behind a Preview button. - Splits now recover across displays, Spaces and new windows. A fixed-size window no longer leaves a hole, and a window that landed off its slot is never resized while others settle. - Undo now undoes the latest command you started, including a move still under way, and ends any split recovery in progress. - Window moves report honestly when they fail, and placements are checked after each move. - Shortcut recorders no longer clash, and there is a display picker. - Reliability: settings load tolerates damaged files, settings save on quit, and the keyboard tap and window watchers recover on their own. - VoiceOver, confirmations and wording polished throughout.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.25
item.description: - Splits are now learned only from changes you make with the mouse. An app resizing its own window (such as Finder), or macOS moving windows after sleep or a Space switch, no longer saves a split. That could leave a big empty space in the middle that Tile and closing windows kept putting back. - Tile now says "Already in your split" when the windows are already in their split, instead of "Tiled" with nothing moving.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.24
item.description:
## Splits, hotkeys and the shortcut card
- **A quit app comes back to its split when you reopen it.** If you quit an app that sat beside other windows, the window left behind grows to fill the space. Reopening the app now puts it back beside that window, in your remembered split when there is one. Before, with Settings › Splits › Make room on set to "Displays already tiled", the reopened app opened on top of the window instead. - **The menu no longer shows hotkeys while they're switched off.** With Settings › Shortcuts › Use global hotkeys off, the menu still listed each item's hotkey, so they seemed to work only while the menu was open. Turn the switch on and hotkeys work in every app. - **The shortcut confirmation shows its full text.** Messages such as "Tiled 3 windows · your split" were cut off at the end.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.23
item.description:
## Splits: new windows tile in more reliably, with an optional wait
- **Apps that take a while to open now tile into their remembered split.** WhatsApp, Wispr Flow, Dia and other apps can take several seconds to show their first window after launch. Tessera used to stop looking before the window appeared, so it opened floating on top of your tiled windows. It now keeps looking for up to 12 seconds. - **New setting: Settings › Splits › Wait before tiling a new app.** Enter a number of seconds (0–60). A window from apps you haven't arranged together before is tiled in equal shares only if it's still open when the wait ends, so an app you open for a moment (Wispr Flow, Finder) is left alone. Apps you've arranged together before get their remembered split straight away. 0 (the default) tiles right away. Search Settings for "wait" or "delay" to find it.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.22
item.description:
## Splits: closing a window fills its space more reliably
- **Closing a window now fills its space even when the window came back late or in its old spot.** Apps such as Wispr Flow reopen exactly where Tessera last tiled them, or show their window a moment after you switch to them. Tessera used to miss those windows, so closing one left an empty column. It now picks them up and re-tiles the rest into your remembered split. - **New setting: Settings › Splits › When a window closes but its app keeps running.** Choose *Re-tile remaining windows* (the default) or *Leave the space empty* for apps that stay in the Dock after you click the close button. Search Settings for "close button" or "dock" to find it.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.21
item.description:
## Menu bar: Columns submenu fits the display you're on
- **The Columns submenu lists only the counts your front window's display allows**, instead of a fixed 2–8 on every screen that quietly clamped. - **The current count is ticked**, so you can see how many columns the display uses. - **One More / One Fewer Column grey out at the ends of the range**, so they never do nothing. - While Tessera finds the front window, the submenu briefly shows "Finding Front Window…"; with no window in front it says "No Window in Front".

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.20
item.description:
## Settings search: results drop down, flip switches in place
- **Search sits in the middle of the title bar** ("Search Tessera", **⌘F**). Results now drop down under it instead of replacing the sidebar, which stays where it is. - Results are grouped by pane under its icon, with the words you typed in bold and where each setting lives. - **On/off settings have their own switch in the results.** Click it, or press **⌥↩**, to change the setting without leaving the search. - **↑ ↓** move, **↩** opens the setting's pane with the row highlighted, **esc** clears. Click back into the field to see the results again. - The sidebar ends with Tessera's icon, name and version; click it for About.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.19
item.description:
## Settings sidebar: fits its names, resizes, blends in
- The sidebar now shares the window's background, so it no longer looks like a separate grey panel. - It is narrower, sized to fit the longest pane name in full at your Mac's sidebar text size. - **Drag its edge** to make it wider, or narrower down to that fitted width. Keep dragging and it switches to icons only; drag back out to see names again. Your width is remembered. - The search field shows its **⌘F** shortcut until you start typing. - Search results wrap onto more lines instead of being cut off.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.18
item.description:
## Settings sidebar: docked icons, a smooth switch, search in the title bar
- **Icons only** is now a slim column docked to the window's edge, with the groups close together. - Switching between names and icons (**⌃⌘S**) now glides instead of snapping. - **Search** sits at the right end of the title bar, one click away in either mode (**⌘F** still works). Typing while only icons show opens the matching settings; clearing the search returns to icons. - The title bar is slimmer, and pane icons no longer have a white outline. - The sidebar's edge can no longer be dragged; use the sidebar button to switch.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.17
item.description:
## Settings sidebar: names or icons
- A sidebar button now sits beside the **Tessera Settings** title (**⌃⌘S**). It switches the sidebar between pane names and icons only; hover an icon to see its name. Tessera remembers your choice. - The sidebar can no longer disappear. Dragging its edge closed now leaves the icons showing. - With icons only, the magnifying glass at the top (or **⌘F**) widens the sidebar for searching.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.16
item.description:
## Splits, organised by display
- **Settings › Splits** now shows one row per display: its name, how many splits Tessera has learned there, and **Manage…**. Stays tidy with one monitor or many; disconnected displays are marked "Not connected". - **Manage…** opens that display's splits in a sheet: app icons and names, when each was learned, and search by app. - Forget one split with its ⊖ button, select several and press Delete, or forget everything on that display. Forgetting several asks first.
## Ring picker glides
- In **Ring › Directions**, a soft highlight now glides around the ring as you hover between layouts, taking the short way round, and the layout under it lifts slightly. - The keyboard focus (← →) glides the same way. - With Reduce Motion on, the highlight moves without animating.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.15
item.description:
## Settings, reorganised
Settings is now grouped by what you're doing:
- **General** - **Controls:** Ring, Shortcuts, Cycles, Excluded Apps - **Windows:** Displays, Splits - **Look:** Appearance (formerly Overlay), Motion - **Updates** and **About**
⌘1–9 follow the new order; ⌘0 opens About.
- The keys that open the ring now live at the top of **Ring**. Ring covers how the ring behaves; how it looks (show the ring, icons, grid lines) is in **Appearance**. - Ring colours have one home: **Appearance › Ring colours**. - Much less text. Short lines under each pane title, and an ⓘ beside a section when you want the details. Warnings still show where they matter. - **About:** a copy icon beside the version replaces the Copy version button. - Settings search finds every setting in its new place.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.14
item.description:
## Settings sidebar fits the search field
The Settings sidebar opened too narrow, so the search field cut off the first letter of "Search settings". The sidebar now opens at a comfortable width and never gets narrow enough to clip the field.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.13
item.description:
## Search your settings
A search field at the top of the Settings sidebar finds any setting from a rough description, such as "remove gap between tiled apps". Pick a result, or use ↑ ↓ and Return, and Settings opens the pane, scrolls to the setting and highlights it.
- ⌘F focuses the field. Esc or the clear button brings the pane list back. - Typos, half-typed words and everyday words (spacing, gap, gutter) all work. - On Macs with Apple Intelligence turned on, a search written as a sentence is also read by Apple's on-device model. Nothing leaves your Mac. General › App › **Understand searches with Apple Intelligence** turns this off.
## Updates have their own pane
Settings › **Updates** holds every update control: Last checked, Check Now, how often to check, automatic install and beta versions. It has its own Restore Defaults.
- If Tessera was replaced while it was open, a check now says to quit and reopen Tessera, instead of failing with "Update Error!".
## Menu bar icons
- The icon you pick now always shows. While hotkeys are paused, a small pause disc sits in its corner instead of replacing it. - Eight new icons drawn in the app icon's tile style: Tiles, Badge, Slot, Mosaic, Ring, Split, Columns and Quarters. Your saved choice carries over to the nearest new icon.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.12
item.description:
## Opening a window makes room
When an app opens a window beside windows that are already tiled side by side, Tessera tiles them again with the new window. If you've taught a split for those apps, they go back to it. Otherwise each window gets an equal share. Adjust them by hand, and Tessera remembers that split for those apps next time.
- A "Made room for …" card explains what happened. ⌃⌥Z undoes it. - Settings › Splits › **Make room when a window opens** turns this on or off. It's on by default. - **Make room on** has two options: - **Displays already tiled** is the default. - **Also wherever the apps have a split** also arranges a display when you open an app you've taught a split for. - Unhiding an app or switching Spaces never rearranges your windows. - A window opened inside an app that's already in front (⌘N) isn't tiled in yet.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.11
item.description: ## Fixed - The Settings title bar is now the same height on every pane. Switching away from Excluded Apps no longer leaves the sidebar partly hidden under the title bar. - The Excluded Apps filter now sits at the top of the app list and appears once at least one app is excluded.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.10
item.description:
## Fixed - Grid layouts with a very large gap no longer place windows outside the usable area of the display.
## Other - Tessera is now licensed under GPL-3.0, with privacy and security notices included. - README updated with screenshots and a short release procedure.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.9
item.description: - Changed: the ring always shows its wedge icons. Ring › Appearance › Layout icons offers Layout pictures or Arrows; "None" is gone, because it left the ring (and the Ring pane's wedge picker) blank. If you had chosen None, you'll see layout pictures again. - Changed: About's icon in Settings is pink, so it no longer looks like General's.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.8
item.description: - Fixed: windows that sit with a gap between them (for example after macOS restores them at login) now close it the first time you drag an edge. Before, "Resize neighbours to fill the display" did nothing across a gap, and Tessera saved the gap as part of your split. - Splits already saved with a gap stay until your next adjustment, or until you forget them in Settings › Splits.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.7
item.description: - New: the menu bar menu shows each item's hotkey at the right edge, such as ⌃⌥T for Tile All Windows and ⌃⌥Z for Undo Last Move, so you can learn them from the menu. A hotkey you change shows the next time the menu opens. - New: Settings › General › Menu bar › Show each item's shortcut (on by default) hides them.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.6
item.description: - New: closing a window no longer leaves a gap. When a window that sits side by side with others closes (or its app quits), the rest cover its space straight away: the apps left go back to the split you taught Tessera for them, or, without one, the window beside the space you used last grows into it. A column beside a closed column widens together. ⌃⌥Z puts the windows back. - New: Settings › Splits › Fill the space when a window closes (on by default) turns it off. - New: setup has a "Tiling that remembers" step, and a tip explains the first gap Tessera fills.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.5
item.description: - New: What Just Happened? Press ⌃⌥/ (or choose What Just Happened? in the menu bar) and a card explains Tessera's last move: which windows it tiled, whether it used your learned split, and what to press to change it. ‹ and › step through the last 10 events. From the command line: `tessera explain`. - New: tips that appear on their own. The first time you tile, and when Tessera does something you might not expect (such as tiling with a split you taught it), a card points at the windows and explains what happened. The first Tile card can walk you through dragging an edge: the neighbours follow, Tessera saves the split, and Undo puts the old split back. - New: buttons on the card for Tile Evenly Instead, Forget This Split and Undo. - Turn tips off, or stop the screen dimming behind them, in Settings › General › Help.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.4
item.description: - Fixed: neighbours now fill the space without a Tile first. Snap windows side by side any way you like (Ring, shortcuts, menu) and resizing one makes the windows beside it follow, from launch onwards. It keeps working after Undo, a display change, sleep and wake, and Tile Evenly. Tile Evenly still never overwrites your learned split.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.3
item.description: - New: neighbours fill the space. After a Tile, resize or move one window and the windows beside it follow its new edges, so no part of the display is left empty. The new arrangement is remembered as your split. Turn it off in Settings › Splits › "Resize neighbours to fill the display". - Fixed: one ⌃⌥Z after a Tile now undoes only the Tile's own moves, and every window undoes in the order it moved, even if you moved a window with a shortcut while the Tile was still gliding.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.2
item.description: - New: Tile Evenly. Tiles every window on a display in equal shares, ignoring your learned split without forgetting it. Find it in the menu bar under Snap, in Shortcuts, App Intents, AppleScript, `tessera tile evenly` and `tessera://tile/evenly`.

item.title: Tessera 0.2.0-beta.1
item.description:
## Tessera 0.2.0 beta 1
The first beta delivered through Tessera's built-in updater.
**New**
- **Check for Updates.** It's in About, the menu bar menu and General → Updates. Tessera checks on the schedule you choose (daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly), shows these notes, and installs only updates signed with Tessera's key. Turn on "Include beta versions" to receive betas like this one. - **Update cue.** When an automatic check finds an update, a dot appears on the menu bar icon and the menu item reads "Update Available…". - **Learned splits.** After Tile or Remember Split, Tessera learns how you adjust a display's windows and reuses those sizes next time. Manage them in Settings → Splits. - **Icon-only Ring**, with an action caption and shortcut receipts.
**Changed**
- About has its own pane (⌘0).
This beta isn't notarised. On a Mac that hasn't run Tessera before, Control-click the app and choose Open the first time.
